title: Unified plan comparison page across app and web
overview: Unified plan comparison page across app and web for Nimbus Wireless customers on app or web. Headline ask: A single plan comparison page with the same layout and plan attributes on app and web. This spec captures 7 functional and 3 non-functional requirements, 4 tracking events, the rollout and test plan, and the open questions the request leaves unanswered (section 15).
problem_statement: Today the app shows plans as a carousel of cards while the website has a comparison table, and the two show different plan attributes. Customers who start on one surface and finish on the other get confused. Analytics cannot compare the two funnels because the events are named differently on each platform. We'd like to run this as an experiment against the current pages.
goals: Increase plan change conversion from the comparison page
Get one funnel for app and web
non_goals: Changing plan prices or creating new plans
Prepaid plans (Nimbus Prepaid will follow later)

functional_requirements.description: A single plan comparison page with the same layout and plan attributes on app and web.
Customers must be able to select up to 3 plans to compare side by side.
Show monthly price, data allowance, hotspot allowance and included perks for each plan.
Customers must be able to filter plans by number of lines.
Selecting a plan must take the customer to the existing plan change checkout.
Plan content must come from the Plan Catalog API so app and web never disagree.
Use the same event names on both platforms.

non_functional_requirements.description: The page should be fast and look modern, with better accessibility [measurable target for 'fast', 'modern', 'better' TBD: OQ-2].
All new UI on app or web meets WCAG 2.1 AA (screen-reader labels, 4.5:1 contrast, full keyboard/switch access).
Tracking events contain zero PII: no names, phone numbers, free-text message content or full account/card numbers.

analytics.naming_convention: snake_case <object>_<action>; action is a past-tense verb (viewed, selected, submitted…)

global_properties.name: platform
global_properties.description: Surface the event fired on (app or web)

global_properties.name: brand
global_properties.description: Brand the customer account belongs to

events.name: plan_comparison_viewed
events.description: The plan comparison is displayed to the customer
events.trigger: Fires once per page load when the plan comparison is at least 50% in the viewport

properties.name: entry_point
properties.description: Screen or link the customer came from

events.name: plan_comparison_plan_selected
events.description: Customer selected an item to compare or buy
events.trigger: Customer taps the select control on an item card

properties.name: position
properties.description: 1-based position of the item on the page

events.name: plan_comparison_filter_applied
events.trigger: Filter value changes and results re-render

events.name: plan_comparison_failed
events.description: The plan comparison could not load or return a result
events.trigger: Client receives an error or a timeout from the backing service

success_metrics.name: Increase plan change conversion from the comparison page
success_metrics.definition: Sessions with `plan_comparison_plan_selected` ÷ sessions with `plan_comparison_viewed`, split by platform

success_metrics.name: Get one funnel for app and web
success_metrics.definition: Share of `plan_comparison_viewed` → `plan_comparison_plan_selected` funnel volume reported from identical event names on app and web (split by `platform`); 100% when no platform-specific events remain

data_model_changes.description: Register the new tracking events; update the modified ones: plan_comparison_viewed.

api_changes.description: PROPOSED client-facing read endpoint backed by Plan Catalog API (A-3); confirm contract, auth and caching.

dependencies.name: Plan Catalog API
dependencies.description: Plan content must come from the Plan Catalog API so app and web never disagree

dependencies.name: Analytics / event dictionary owners
dependencies.description: Review new and modified events before release.

edge_cases.scenario: Plan Catalog API times out or returns an error
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Show a non-blocking error state, let the customer continue, and fire `plan_comparison_failed` with error_code.

edge_cases.scenario: Customer tries to select more than 3 items
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Selection beyond 3 is blocked with an inline message.

edge_cases.scenario: A filter combination returns no results
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Show an empty state with a reset action.

edge_cases.scenario: Customer in a group whose eligibility is unresolved (OQ-1: Can logged-out visitors see the page?)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Behaviour follows the answer to OQ-1; until it is resolved the feature stays hidden for that group.

edge_cases.scenario: Customer starts on app and finishes on web (or vice versa)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Same content on both; events keep identical names and differ only in `platform`.

edge_cases.scenario: Analytics is blocked or consent is declined
edge_cases.expected_behavior: The feature works normally; no events are sent and no errors are shown.

experiment.primary_metric: Increase plan change conversion from the comparison page

risks.description: Event names drift between app and web, breaking the cross-platform funnel
risks.mitigation: Treat section 7 as the single source; lint against the event dictionary in CI.

risks.description: Plan Catalog API latency or outage degrades the experience
risks.mitigation: Timeouts with graceful fallback; alert on the failed-event rate.

risks.description: 1 blocking open question(s) delay build start
risks.mitigation: Review open questions with owners before sprint planning.

risks.description: Experiment is under-powered for the expected effect
risks.mitigation: Size the test once the MDE is agreed.

assumptions.statement: Accessibility follows the company default of WCAG 2.1 AA.
Analytics events must not carry PII; this is standard instrumentation policy.
API contracts below are placeholders until the owning team confirms them.
Rollout stages follow the standard flag-based ramp.

open_questions.question: Can logged-out visitors see the page?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The request explicitly leaves this open; it changes scope or eligibility logic.

open_questions.question: What measurable target defines 'fast', 'modern', 'better' in: "The page should be fast and look modern, with better accessibility"?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without a threshold the requirement cannot be tested or accepted.

open_questions.question: What is the target and timeframe for: "Increase plan change conversion from the comparison page"?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Success metrics need a target to size the rollout and judge the launch.

open_questions.question: What is the target and timeframe for: "Get one funnel for app and web"?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Success metrics need a target to size the rollout and judge the launch.

open_questions.question: What are the primary metric, minimum detectable effect and planned duration of the experiment?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Needed to size the test and decide when to stop it.

open_questions.question: Is `plan_comparison_plan_selected` the same user action as existing `PlanCompare_Select`? If so, reuse the existing event.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Avoids two events for one action, which double-counts the funnel.

open_questions.question: Property 'monthly_price' is 'number' here but 'string' in the dictionary (on 'PlanCompare_Select'). Align the type or version the property?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Conflicting types break joins and dashboards across events.
